claims.text: The target high-entropy alloys are in the solid phase at room temperature.
A machine-learning model trained on existing thermodynamic data can accurately predict melting temperatures of high-entropy alloys.
A machine-learning model trained on existing thermodynamic data can accurately predict enthalpies of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
A machine-learning model trained on existing thermodynamic data can accurately predict entropies of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
A machine-learning model trained on existing thermodynamic data can accurately predict volume changes at melting for high-entropy alloys.
The proposed model uses compositional data and existing experimental results as predictive inputs or training information.
The model will be trained on a diverse dataset of high-entropy alloys with known thermodynamic properties.
The training data will cover a wide range of compositions and processing conditions.
High-entropy-alloy composition influences thermodynamic behavior.
Atomic arrangement in high-entropy alloys influences thermodynamic behavior.
Machine-learning algorithms can identify complex patterns and correlations in thermodynamic training data.
Patterns in the data relate alloy composition to thermodynamic properties.
Learning composition-property correlations enables accurate thermodynamic-property predictions.
Predictions of melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, and volume change at melting will be within ±5% of experimental values.
Current experimental methods for determining the target thermodynamic properties are time-consuming.
Current experimental methods for determining the target thermodynamic properties are resource-intensive.
The model is expected to be applicable to high-entropy alloys compositionally similar to the training data.
The model may not generalize to alloys with compositions substantially different from the training data.
The model may not generalize to alloys with structures substantially different from those represented in the training data.
The model may overfit its training data.
